title: Pattern Headings: Musical Compositions
summary: Pattern list for headings for musical compositions (forms and types, medium of performance, style, function, occasions, settings of special texts, and headings with --Hymns, --Music, --Musical settings, --Songs and music; pattern heading Operas). Gives the free-floating qualifier ", Arranged" for instrumental music, rules for geographic and chronological subdivisions (fixed $y century list, not for jazz/popular, folk/non-Western, single-composer collections, or individual works), the treatment of paired singular/plural headings (e.g. Opera/Operas) with --History and criticism, the subdivision order geographic-chronological-topical-form, and three lists of free-floating subdivisions with endnote restrictions.
validation_rules: Headings in this category are those for musical forms and types of compositions, medium of performance, style, function, music for special seasons or occasions, musical settings of special texts, etc., and headings including the subdivisions `--Hymns`, `--Music`, `--Musical settings`, `--Songs and music` (e.g. `Sonatas (Oboe)`, `Trios (Piano, flute, violin)`, `Rock music`, `Easter music`, `Magnificat (Music)`, `Catholic Church--Hymns`, `African Americans--Music`, `French poetry--Musical settings`, `Baseball--Songs and music`). The general heading `Music` is not in this category. (H 1160, Types of headings)

Any subdivision on these lists is free-floating under any heading in the category if appropriate and no conflict exists in the subject authority file; established variant phrases/subdivisions may exist and take precedence. (H 1160, Conflicts)

`, Arranged` is a free-floating qualifier appended (comma + space) to headings for arranged instrumental music, e.g. `Piano music, Arranged`; `Variations (Violin and piano), Arranged`. (H 1160 sec. 2.a)
For vocal music, a heading with `, Arranged` is valid only if that heading has been established; it is not free-floating. (H 1160 sec. 2.b)

For arranged excerpts, do not use `, Arranged` on the heading; use the subdivision `--Excerpts, Arranged` with the basic heading, e.g. `Suites (Violin and piano)--Excerpts, Arranged`. (H 1160 sec. 2.c)

Geographic subdivision brings out origin of the music or nationality of composers for collections and topical materials, only when geographic focus is stated or implied in the title or series; do not use geographic subdivisions for collections of works by one composer. (H 1160 sec. 3)

The only chronological subdivisions for this category are `--To 500`, `--500-1400`, `--15th century`, `--16th century`, `--17th century`, `--18th century`, `--19th century`, `--20th century`, `--21st century`. (H 1160 sec. 4)

Do not use these chronological subdivisions for jazz and popular music (see H 1916.5), in headings for folk or non-Western music (see H 1917), for collections of works by one composer, for individual musical works, or following the subdivisions `--Hymns`, `--Music`, `--Musical settings`, `--Songs and music`. (H 1160 sec. 4)

Where separate headings exist for the compositions (usually plural) and for works about them (usually singular), e.g. `Operas`/`Opera`, `Sonatas`/`Sonata`, `Symphonies`/`Symphony`, `Choruses`/`Choral music`, `Sacred music`/`Church music`, do not use `--History and criticism` under either form. Separate singular and plural terms are no longer established. (H 1160 sec. 5.a, 5.b(2))
Otherwise use `--History and criticism` under headings for musical compositions for works about them when no more specific subdivision applies. (H 1160 sec. 5.b(1))

When a medium of performance is added in a parenthetical qualifier to form a heading for literature about the form, use the plural form of the main term, which may then take `--History and criticism`: `Concertos (Piano)--History and criticism`, not `Concerto (Piano)`. (H 1160 sec. 5.b(2))

Subdivisions other than `--History and criticism` go under the term for the compositions unless the item clearly calls for the term for materials about them (e.g. `Operas--Analysis, appreciation`; `Operas--Bibliography--Catalogs`; `Opera--Bibliography`). (H 1160 sec. 5.c)

Subdivisions on Lists 1-3 may be used under headings for collections and individual works, under specific form/genre headings, and under `Chamber music`, `Dramatic music`, `Instrumental music`, `Sacred vocal music`, `Vocal music`. Since February 2024 there are no further limitations on List 1 subdivisions. (H 1160 sec. 6 and note 7)

Order of subdivisions for musical compositions is: geographic, chronological, topical, form, e.g. `Gregorian chants--Italy--Piacenza--500-1400--Manuscripts--Congresses`; `Symphonies--Italy, Northern--19th century--Scores`. (H 1160 sec. 7)
Musical presentation form subdivisions may follow `--Excerpts` / `--Excerpts, Arranged`, e.g. `Symphonies--Excerpts, Arranged--Scores and parts`. (H 1160 sec. 7, note 2)
`--Parts (solo)`, `--Scores and parts (solo)`, and all `--Solo with ...` / `--Solos with ...` subdivisions are valid for instrumental music only. (H 1160 note 1)

`--Excerpts` and `--Excerpts, Arranged` are used only under headings for form or type of composition; do not use `--Excerpts` if the music has also been arranged for a different medium — use `--Excerpts, Arranged`. (H 1160 note 2)
`--Juvenile` (List 2) is not valid if `--Juvenile sound recordings` is used. (H 1160 note 3)

`--Texts`, `--History and criticism`, `--Production and direction`, and `--Religious aspects` are not valid under headings for which a separate singular topical heading exists for resources about the works (e.g. `Opera`, `Oratorio`). (H 1160 note 4)

`--Religious aspects` is not valid under headings for forms (e.g. `Sonatas`), headings with medium of performance (e.g. `Violin music`, `Concertos (Flute)`), or headings where religious function is implied (e.g. `Te Deum laudamus (Music)`, `Wedding music`). (H 1160 note 5)

`--Religious aspects` may be further subdivided by a religion or Christian denomination (e.g. `Popular music--Religious aspects--Islam`); each such heading must be editorially established. See H 1998. (H 1160 note 6)
`--First performances`, `--Instruction and study`, `--Performances`, and `--Production and direction` may be subdivided geographically; other subdivisions on the lists may not. (H 1160 sec. 8)
Most `$v` form subdivisions on Lists 2 and 3 may also be used as `$x` topical subdivisions for works about the form. (H 1160 sec. 8, list notes)
[LC practice] An exceptional variant form to be retained gets a UF reference from the free-floating form (H 195); otherwise propose a change (H 193). (H 1160, Conflicts)

sections.heading: 1. General rule
sections.text: The free-floating subdivisions listed here may be used as appropriate under headings for collections of music, individual musical works, and literature and other materials about music, according to the instructions provided.

sections.heading: 2. Arranged works
sections.text: For additional instructions about arranged works, see also H 1917.5, sec. 7.

sections.heading: a. Instrumental music
sections.text:
Use “, Arranged” as a free-floating qualifier with headings for arranged instrumental music to indicate that the medium of performance specified represents an arrangement and not the original instrumentation. Examples:

```
650 $0 $a Piano music, Arranged.
650 $0 $a Variations (Violin and piano), Arranged.
```

sections.heading: b. Vocal music
sections.text: When use of “, Arranged” is permitted for vocal music, the heading incorporating it must be established.

sections.heading: c. Exception: arranged excerpts
sections.text:
For arranged excerpts, use the subdivision –Excerpts, Arranged with the basic heading. Example:

```
650 #0 $a Suites (Violin and piano) $v Excerpts, Arranged.
```

sections.heading: 3. Geographic subdivisions
sections.text:
Use geographic subdivisions to bring out the origin of the music or the nationality of the composers in collections of musical works, and for topical materials. Use them only when geographic focus is stated or implied in the title or series statement of the item being cataloged. Use a geographic subdivision under the most specific heading that is applicable to all or most of the works in the collection. Assign other headings that may also be appropriate without geographic subdivision.

Do not use geographic subdivisions for collections of works by one composer.

sections.heading: 4. Chronological subdivisions
sections.text:
Use the chronological subdivisions listed below to bring out the period represented in collections of musical works, and for topical materials. Use them only when chronological focus is stated or implied in the title or series statement of the item being cataloged. Use a chronological subdivision under the most specific heading that is applicable to all or most of the works in the collection. Assign other headings that may also be appropriate without chronological subdivision. For general guidance on chronological headings and subdivisions, see H 620. For guidance on the order of subdivisions when chronological subdivisions are used in conjunction with other types, see H 1075.

```
$y To 500
$y 500-1400
$y 15th century
$y 16th century
$y 17th century
$y 18th century
$y 19th century
$y 20th century
$y 21st century
```

Do not use these chronological subdivisions:

- for jazz and popular music (see H 1916.5)
- in headings for folk or non-Western music (see H 1917)
- for collections of works by one composer
- for individual musical works
- following the subdivisions –Hymns; –Music; –Musical settings; and –Songs and music

sections.heading: 5. Topical and form subdivisions for literature about music
a. Previous practice for headings: two different terms for similar concepts
sections.text:
For some forms and types of compositions, separate terms, usually the singular and plural, have been established for literature and other materials about the form or type and for the compositions themselves. Separate singular and plural terms are no longer established. Check the subject authority file for headings of this type before adding subdivisions for works about musical compositions. For instructions on the formulation of new form/genre headings for musical compositions, see H 1917.5.

Examples of older headings:

| Headings for musical compositions | Headings for works about the compositions |
|---|---|
| Operas | Opera |
| Sonatas | Sonata |
| Symphonies | Symphony |

In some cases, the two terms are entirely different. Example:

| Heading for musical compositions | Heading for works about the compositions |
|---|---|
| Choruses | Choral music |
| Sacred music | Church music |

sections.heading: b. The topical subdivision –History and criticism for works about musical compositions
sections.text:
(1) General rule. Use the subdivision –History and criticism under headings for musical compositions if no more specific subdivision is appropriate for works about them.

(2) Exceptions. When separate headings have been established for musical compositions and for works about them, do not use the subdivision –History and criticism under either form of the heading. When extending the main heading by adding a medium of performance in a parenthetical qualifier in order to formulate a suitable heading for literature about the form or type, use the plural form of the main term. Headings of this kind may be subdivided by –History and criticism.

Example:

```
Title: Mozart’s piano concertos.
650 #0 $a Concertos (Piano) $x History and criticism.
  [not 650 #0 $a Concerto (Piano)]
```

sections.heading: c. Other topical and form subdivisions
sections.text:
When adding subdivisions other than –History and criticism to headings for forms, types, etc., of musical works where different terms have been established for the compositions themselves and for literature or other materials about them, add the subdivision to the term for the compositions unless it is clear from the item being cataloged that the subdivision should be added to the term for materials about them. Examples:

```
650 #0 $a Choral music $v Bibliography.
650 #0 $a Choruses, Sacred $v Discography.

650 #0 $a Opera $v Bibliography.
650 #0 $a Operas $x Analysis, appreciation.
650 #0 $a Operas $v Bibliography $v Catalogs.
650 #0 $a Operas $v Thematic catalogs.
```

sections.heading: 6. Form subdivisions for musical presentation and medium of performance
sections.text:
Use the free-floating subdivisions on Lists 1-3 below under headings assigned to collections of musical works and to individual works. Use the subdivisions under specific form/genre headings and under the following collective headings.[^7]

```
150 ## $a Chamber music
150 ## $a Dramatic music
150 ## $a Instrumental music
150 ## $a Sacred vocal music
150 ## $a Vocal music
```

sections.heading: 7. Order of subdivisions
sections.text:
The basic order of subdivisions for musical compositions is: geographic, chronological, topical, form. For further guidance on geographic and chronological subdivisions, see H 870, sec. 3.a. Examples:

```
650 #0 $a Gregorian chants $x Accompaniments $x Instruction and study.
650 #0 $a Gregorian chants $z Italy $z Piacenza $y 500-1400 $x Manuscripts $v Congresses.
650 #0 $a Instrumental music $v Bibliography $v Graded lists.
650 #0 $a Instrumental music $y 18th century $x History and criticism $v Periodicals.
650 #0 $a Instrumental music $y 18th century $x Interpretation (Phrasing, dynamics, etc.)
650 #0 $a Keyboard instrument music $z France $y 17th century $x History and criticism.
650 #0 $a Piano music $z Brazil $y 20th century $v Bibliography.
650 #0 $a Sacred vocal music $z Austria $z Lambach (Upper Austria) $y 18th century $x Manuscripts $v Thematic catalogs.
650 #0 $a Sacred vocal music $z Brazil $z Minas Gerais $y 19th century $v Bibliography.
650 #0 $a Symphonies $z Italy, Northern $y 19th century $v Scores.
650 #0 $a Symphonies $v Excerpts, Arranged $v Scores and parts.
```

sections.heading: NOTES
sections.text:
1. Valid for instrumental music only.
2. Use only under headings for form or type of composition. Do not use the subdivision –Excerpts if the music has also been arranged for a medium of performance different from the original; instead, use the subdivision –Excerpts, Arranged. May be further subdivided by other musical presentation subdivisions.
3. Not valid if the subdivision –Juvenile sound recordings (cf. H 1690) is used.
4. Not valid under headings for which there is a separate topical heading in the singular, e.g. Opera; Oratorio, for resources about those musical works.
5. Not valid under headings for forms, e.g., Sonatas; headings with medium of performance, e.g., Violin music; Concertos (Flute); or headings where religious function is implied, e.g., Te Deum laudamus (Music); Wedding music.
6. May be subdivided topically by a religion or Christian denomination. Editorially establish each heading of the type that is so subdivided, e.g., Popular music–Religious aspects–Islam; Popular music–Religious aspects–United Methodist Church. For instructions on the use of the subdivision, see H 1998.
7. A change in policy occurred February 2024, which removed the limitations on the application of subdivisions from List 1.

[^7]: See note 7.

list.scope: Free-floating subdivisions usable under headings for musical forms and types of compositions, medium of performance, style, function, music for special seasons or occasions, musical settings of special texts, and headings with the subdivisions –Hymns, –Music, –Musical settings, –Songs and music (not the general heading Music). Lists 1-3 are usable under headings for collections of musical works and individual works, specific form/genre headings, and Chamber music; Dramatic music; Instrumental music; Sacred vocal music; Vocal music.
general_notes: Any subdivision listed here can be used as a free-floating subdivision under any heading belonging to the category if it is appropriate and no conflict exists in the subject authority file.  Headings employing variant phrases or subdivisions equivalent to subdivisions on the lists given here may be found in the subject authority file.

Basic order of subdivisions for musical compositions: geographic, chronological, topical, form. (sec. 7)
Do not use geographic subdivisions for collections of works by one composer. (sec. 3)
